raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Leaving Pont Neuf behind, head for Notre-Dame Cathedral, about an 18-minute walk away.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The Revolution that melted the Pont-Neuf king struck down the stone kings here too.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":1},{"text":"You're standing on the Parvis, the wide, windswept square in front of the cathedral.","source_id":"795e33c7-62ec-45bf-8924-1f7da57be4c7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Haussmann cleared it in the 1860s, and its name comes from an old word for paradise.","source_id":"795e33c7-62ec-45bf-8924-1f7da57be4c7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"It was inside these walls, in 1804, that Napoleon set the crown on his own head and made himself emperor.","source_id":"58756a99-4b2f-47ff-acef-d815518d628f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The church was so run-down by then that its crumbling walls had to be hidden behind drapes just to look grand enough.","source_id":"58756a99-4b2f-47ff-acef-d815518d628f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"It rears up from the Île de la Cité like a great ship moored by huge flying buttresses.","source_id":"58756a99-4b2f-47ff-acef-d815518d628f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["795e33c7-62ec-45bf-8924-1f7da57be4c7"]},{"text":"This is the symbolic heart of France.","source_id":"795e33c7-62ec-45bf-8924-1f7da57be4c7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"It went up on far older ground, first a Roman temple to Jupiter.","source_id":"58756a99-4b2f-47ff-acef-d815518d628f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"On top of that came the Merovingian cathedral of St-Etienne, and then the Gothic church you see today.","source_id":"58756a99-4b2f-47ff-acef-d815518d628f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Work began in 1160 under Bishop de Sully and was finished around 1345.","source_id":"58756a99-4b2f-47ff-acef-d815518d628f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Its seminaries became an ecclesiastical powerhouse, turning out six popes across the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.","source_id":"58756a99-4b2f-47ff-acef-d815518d628f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Later it lost ground to rival sees like Rheims and St-Denis, and the building slid into decline.","source_id":"58756a99-4b2f-47ff-acef-d815518d628f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The facade is the cathedral's most impressive exterior feature.","source_id":"95354cf4-b2c6-4efe-8be6-16049d093bba","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"You can still read the older Romanesque style in its solid H-shape, but the filigree of the central rose window and the gallery above lifts the whole front into lightness and grace.","source_id":"95354cf4-b2c6-4efe-8be6-16049d093bba","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"That row of 27 huge figures beneath the rose window isn't French royalty at all — they're the biblical kings, the ancestors of Christ.","source_id":"8b453722-4367-424e-a58b-c452f6efaa9b","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"During the Revolution, enthusiasts mistook them for France's own kings and tore them down, so every statue up there now is a copy.","source_id":"8b453722-4367-424e-a58b-c452f6efaa9b","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["58756a99-4b2f-47ff-acef-d815518d628f"]},{"text":"Over the central doorway sits the most arresting carving of all, the Day of Judgement.","source_id":"f9fffe53-2022-411b-88a8-261f806e19d6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"In the lower frieze the dead climb from their graves in a whirl of movement, while Christ presides above, sending the souls on his right to heaven and those on his left to hell.","source_id":"f9fffe53-2022-411b-88a8-261f806e19d6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"And around the arch peer small, alert, mischievous angels — said to be modelled on the cathedral's own choirboys.","source_id":"f9fffe53-2022-411b-88a8-261f806e19d6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"By the west door, look down for a small bronze star, a brass stud in the pavement marking the city's Zero Point, or kilometre zero, from which every main-road distance in France is measured.","source_id":"795e33c7-62ec-45bf-8924-1f7da57be4c7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["4361876b-a87a-48fc-ae56-159bc1933823"]},{"text":"People treat it as a wishing stone now, though its real job was always to fix the road to every other town.","source_id":"4361876b-a87a-48fc-ae56-159bc1933823","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"And beneath the square, a crypt holds Gallo-Roman walls, a quay, a hypocaust and medieval cellars — two thousand years of the city stacked in one room.","source_id":"82edc190-920e-47b0-9b5c-69a2ba678e28","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Those white paving blocks set into the square trace the outlines of the little streets and houses that crowded here in medieval times.","source_id":"795e33c7-62ec-45bf-8924-1f7da57be4c7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Back at the Pont-Neuf's eastern end, across from the statue of Henri IV, red-brick seventeenth-century houses flank a narrow entrance.","source_id":"4b8ecfe7-21e2-4cc7-a05c-e0485a7445a4","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"They lead into place Dauphine, one of the city's most secluded and handsome squares.","source_id":"4b8ecfe7-21e2-4cc7-a05c-e0485a7445a4","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"That's the walk — Notre-Dame, the great stone ship at the heart of France.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":1}]}
